summary.title: IPOs and Beyond: A Guide to Exit Options for Companies
summary.one_liner: Learn how IPOs, SPAC mergers, direct listings, M&A and secondary sales compare for startup founders and investors in terms of valuation, dilution, liquidity and timing.
keywords: pipe private investment in public equity
takeaways: IPOs raise new capital through an underwriter-led roadshow and allocation process, and tend to price higher in hot markets.
SPACs are faster but more dilutive and costly because of sponsor promote, warrants and higher fees, and PIPE discounts have grown.
Direct listings sell no new shares and avoid the IPO discount and lock-up, but suit only well-known, well-capitalized companies.
M&A is a true 100% exit but often values a company below what an IPO can achieve in a hot market.
Secondary sales, including company buybacks and third-party tender offers, give employees and investors interim liquidity before an exit.
summary.summary: The article compares the main exit routes for venture-backed companies: traditional IPOs, SPAC mergers, direct listings, M&A and secondary sales. Each section explains how the process works, recent market trends (such as IPO volumes, SPAC activity and M&A volume in 2021), and what the option means for founders and investors. It draws on figures from sources such as Cap IQ, Morgan Stanley, Citi and LionTree. The piece is written from a VC firm's perspective and offers conclusions for each path rather than step-by-step instructions.
